ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Judy Garland

code.originalText: Four-month review: phenobarbital taper, sleep, mood, laboratory checks and the plan to finish

text.paragraph: Four-month review: phenobarbital taper, sleep, mood and laboratory checks. [S]

Ms. Garland returns four weeks after her preventive visit. She lowered phenobarbital to 40.5 mg a day at that visit and to 32.4 mg a day two weeks ago. After the last step she lay awake for three nights and felt shaky inside, without a tremor others could see; it has eased but not fully gone, and she would like to stay at this dose for a while. She has taken no secobarbital, stimulant or other sedative. She sleeps about six hours on most nights. Her mood is good and she is enjoying work again. She eats three meals on most days and says she feels stronger. Her HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests from the preventive visit were nonreactive, and she was told by phone. She wants to talk about stopping smoking once the taper is over. [S]

list.item:
Barbiturate use disorder on a phenobarbital taper (F13.20). From 97.2 to 32.4 mg a day over fourteen weeks without a seizure or a return to secobarbital. The last step brought mild rebound wakefulness, so the taper is paused, as she asked. Urine test shows barbiturates only. Blood count normal; AST 23 and ALT 20 U/L normal; GGT 48 U/L, mildly raised by phenobarbital's effect on the liver's enzymes, to be rechecked after the taper. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]
Hold phenobarbital at 32.4 mg a day for four weeks, then 24.3, 16.2 and 8.1 mg a day, each for two to four weeks, and stop.
Addiction medicine review by video with Dr. Grünewald when the taper ends.
Repeat liver tests three months after stopping.

Stimulant use disorder, mild, in early remission (F15.10). No stimulant for twelve weeks; urine test negative for amphetamine. [S]
No stimulant prescriptions.

Depression with anxious distress on sertraline (F32.1). PHQ-9 5 from 14 and GAD-7 5 from 13: a good response, close to remission. [S]
Continue sertraline 50 mg daily for at least six to twelve months after remission.
Psychotherapy every two weeks.

Chronic insomnia (G47.00). Insomnia Severity Index 10 from 21; about six hours of sleep. [S]
Continue CBT-I every two weeks through the end of the taper.
